messages:
Aisha (Product): Quick question — for the automatic fallback policy UI, can we expose a mapping from SLA signals (p95 latency, error_rate, token budget) to named degrade modes, while keeping an auditable history of triggers and actions?
Ben (EngPlatform): I think so. We already have the decision-service that evaluates rules. Proposal: signals -> rule -> action. Need to decide what signals are first-class and how we show thresholds.
Marta (UX): From a UX POV we should avoid raw metric names. Show friendly labels + example symptoms, e.g. "High latency (p95 > 500ms)". Also preview expected behavior and risk (quality/cost).
Diego (SRE): Ops notes: add hysteresis + cooldown to avoid oscillation. Also we need a safe default: prefer cheaper variant or reduce token window before routing to other regions. And send alerts to #oncall.
Anu (Data): Telemetry: define canonical metric names: model.latency.p95, model.errors_per_min, model.token_consumption.avg. We should include a small sample snapshot in each audit event (last 1m/5m).
Ben (EngPlatform): Sketch of a policy config (for discussion):
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  id: auto-sla-1
  description: "adaptive fallback based on latency/errors"
  triggers:
    - signal: model.latency.p95
      operator: '>'
      value: 500   # milliseconds
      duration: 120  # seconds
      action:
        type: switch_variant
        target: quantized-v2
      cooldown: 300  # seconds
      audit: true
    - signal: model.errors_per_min
      operator: '>'
      value: 10
      duration: 60
      action:
        type: degrade_mode
        target: "reduce_penalty_sampling"
      cooldown: 180
```
Marta (UX): Good start. In the console, expose those fields but also offer presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive). Show an inline simulation for each rule (example request -> expected output).
Aisha (Product): We also need an explicit approval trail: who created the policy, who enabled it, and a link to the telemetry snapshot that triggered each activation. Retention: at least 90 days.
Diego (SRE): Add requirement: any automated fallback must log a unique decision_id and be reversible by the operator. Also include an emergency escape-hatch to disable auto-fallback for a model.
Anu (Data): Implementation note: audit record should include metric values (not just booleans) and the evaluation time window. Sample shape: {metric: value, window_secs: 60}. Keep payload small (<8KB).
Ben (EngPlatform): For determinism we should evaluate rules in the decision-service and persist the decision event to event-store (append-only). Then the router consumes the event to execute action. That keeps audit and execution traceable.
rollout-bot: Canary rollout: policy auto-sla-1 deployed to prod canary (5% traffic) at 1750007000.
Marta (UX): One more: when a rule has low confidence (insufficient telemetry), show a yellow banner and don't auto-execute unless user checks "enable low-data triggers".
Aisha (Product): :thumbsup: Agree. Let's sync tomorrow 10:00am to finalize fields and default presets. Ben — can you create a GH issue with the YAML example, the SRE constraints, and mockups?
Ben (EngPlatform): Will do. I'll open INFRA-4021 and link the mockups. Also adding a test-plan to simulate burst patterns and assert no flip-flop.
Diego (SRE): I'll add load scripts to the test-plan and a runbook snippet for manual rollback.
Anu (Data): I'll add a short query template to extract the telemetry snapshot for the audit record.
Aisha (Product): Thanks all. small follow-ups in the PR.
